findings.message: Criterion 5 asserts that after a Rework escalation, the drain's one re-offer records a retry `cap_consumed` body `{cap: retry, ticket_sha, rung}` carrying the escalated rung. `Drain._run_one` (chupa/drain.py:265-270) gets its rung only from the latest terminal `state_transition` body (`body.get("rung")`) and never reads a `rework_escalate` signal. So the escalated rung can only reach the draw if `chupa/drain.py` is edited. Under the section 9 ownership law, the module that journals `cap_consumed` owns the cap draw, and here that module is the drain. That forced edit is outside `## Scope fence`, and Scope out explicitly says 'Out: ... `chupa/drain.py` retry-draw behavior'. As written, the correct Implement outcome is `premise_failed`.
findings.paved_road: Pick one. (a) Narrow criterion 5 to what Rework owns: the test proves Rework appends exactly one `{signal: rework_escalate, rung}` whose rung equals `caps.next_rung(...)` for the folded `caps.capability`, and that Rework never calls `caps.consume`. Drop the clauses about the drain re-offer, rung reuse, and terminal-body-only rung, and file the drain-side consumption of the escalation rung to the Suggestion Box as a plan gap (no P3 row fences `chupa/drain.py` for it; `rework-activation` is the likely owner). (b) Fence `chupa/drain.py` and `tests/test_drain.py`, move the drain consumption of `rework_escalate` into Scope in, remove it from Scope out and Definition of rejected, and add a behavioral-dormancy test showing no production caller writes the signal. Option (a) keeps the registry row's fence floor intact and is the smaller repair.
